Jasmine —

Thanks for sending the draft order form and the redlined MSA. We've run this past procurement and legal and they have a few items they want clarified on the SLA so the redlines are actionable:

1) Uptime target — the MSA currently references "Availability: 99.9%" but the Order Form table calls out 99.95% for the dedicated model. We need a single canonical metric and the measurement window definition (monthly? rolling 30-day?).

2) Service Credit calc — the example in the spreadsheet seems to prorate credits on total monthly spend. Legal wants the exact formula spelled out (i.e., credit = (1 - measured_availability/target) * monthly_fee capped at X). Also confirm whether credits are the sole remedy.

3) Response times — your support sheet lists P1 = 1 hour and P1 follow-up at 4 hours; our security ops requires an initial phone escalation within 30 minutes for P1 incidents that affect production AI pipelines. Can we make the phone/escalation step explicit?

4) Maintenance window — the MSA allows "reasonable advance notice"; procurement wants a minimum notice period (48 vs 72 hours) for planned maintenance that can impact production and a definition of "emergency maintenance".

We attached a short markup of the Order Form SLA table for your convenience. Can we set up a quick call this week to resolve these so our legal team can sign off?

Regards,
Sarah
Senior Counsel, Acme Energy

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear notes and the spreadsheet markup. Totally reasonable requests. Quick responses inline below — happy to jump on a call; propose Thu 10/1 10:00am PT if that works for you.

1) Uptime target: Our commercial standard for Dedicated capacity is 99.95% measured on a monthly calendar basis. We'll update the MSA to make the Order Form table the canonical source and add the "measurement period = calendar month" language.

2) Service Credits: We agree it should be explicit. Proposed formula we can add to the Order Form: "If Measured Availability < Target Availability for the Measurement Period then Credit = min((Target - Measured)/Target * Monthly Fee, 100% of Monthly Fee). Credits are the exclusive monetary remedy; service credits do not preclude injunctive relief for data breaches or security incidents." Please confirm if the cap at 100% is acceptable or if you require a different cap.

3) Response times: We can commit to the following for Dedicated customers: P1 initial response via ticketing system within 1 hour AND an initial phone escalation to on-call within 30 minutes of ticket creation if the incident is classified as production impacting (customers must tag P1 and provide incident bridge). We'll add phone escalation language and the requirement for customer-provided bridge info in the Order Form.

4) Maintenance: We typically give 72 hours notice for planned maintenance that might affect availability; 48 hours is our min for routine infra work but we can agree to 72 for any maintenance that could cause degraded response. Emergency maintenance (security/preservation) is excluded but we'll commit to an update within 4 hours of occurrence.

Next steps: I'll push a clean MSA with these edits and a revised Order Form SLA table for your review before the call. If Thu 10/1 10am PT doesn't work I'll propose alternates.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Subject: Internal — proposed credit bands and legal language

Team —

Drafting notes for our call with Acme:

- Credit bands (proposed for Dedicated):
  * Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.00% <= Availability < 99.95%: 5% of monthly fee
  * 95.00% <= Availability < 99.00%: 15% of monthly fee
  * Availability < 95.00%: 30% of monthly fee
  * Cap: 100% of monthly fee per measurement period

- Measurement: calendar month; downtime excludes scheduled maintenance (as defined) and force majeure; partial-hour downtimes prorated to the minute.

- Response times: include explicit on-call phone escalation for P1 within 30 minutes; add customer responsibilities to provide bridge and point-of-contact.

- Maintenance notice: propose 72 hours for anything that could affect availability; "emergency maintenance" defined as actions needed to prevent or mitigate active security incidents, with notification within 4 hours post-action.

- Legal: Add "exclusive monetary remedy" clause but leave carveout for security incidents that cause data breach/custodial loss. Recommend we run the final redline through legal to ensure the carveout language is acceptable.

I'll be on the call Friday morning to field legal/ops questions. Dev, can you pull any historical availability numbers for similar Dedicated pools to help Acme model exposures?

Laura
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
